title: adj repos: manage the user repo list
lead: Add adj repos add/remove/list, which manage a per-user list of adj repos in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/adjudicate/config.json, so a later adj inbox --all (S18) can read it.
findings_note: Owner decision 2026-10-18 (S18 config): user config file managed by adj repos add/remove/list
boundary: **Not in this slice:** adj inbox --all and anything that reads the repos for display (S18); any other user setting; changing .adjudicate.json; slicer catalog records (S22 runs in parallel and would take the same catalog id: record C32 decisions as slicer notes on S38; the outer session files them at landing).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Owner decisions 2026-10-18 (S18 cross-repo inbox, split into this slice and S18): the repo list lives in a user config file $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/adjudicate/config.json, falling back to $HOME/.config/adjudicate/config.json when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset or empty (not os.UserConfigDir, which is ~/Library/Application Support on macOS). Shape: {"repos": ["/abs/path", ...]}. adj manages it: adj repos add [PATH] (default: the current repo root; stored as an absolute, cleaned path; must hold .adjudicate.json; a path already listed is a no-op, exit 0), adj repos remove PATH, adj repos list [--json]. Writes are atomic (temp file in the same directory + rename) and create the directory if missing. This is the first file adj writes outside a repo.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/userconfig/ (new package; or internal/store/userconfig.go if that reads better under C32): path resolution from an injected getenv, Load (a missing file is an empty list; unknown keys, a non-absolute path or bad JSON are errors, as store config is strict), Save (atomic, 0644 file, 0755 dir), Add, Remove.
- internal/commands/repos.go (+ test) and internal/cli/repos.go (+ test): the three subcommands; dispatch and usage in internal/cli/cli.go.
- internal/render: list text (one path per line) and JSON ({"repos": [...]}); docs/json.md and internal/cli/jsonshape_test.go pin it.
- README.md, PROJECT.md (Commands; data model: the user config), AGENTS.md (Commands entry, Layout), CHANGELOG.md (## Unreleased).
- internal/commands/ai.md: do not change (agents do not manage the repo list; 1799/1800 bytes).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Table-driven, red first; every test injects XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME through cli.Env.Getenv pointing into t.TempDir(), so no test touches the real home:
- Path resolution: XDG_CONFIG_HOME set; unset or empty falls back to HOME/.config; neither set is an error (exit 1).
- add with no PATH adds the current root (Env.Root / --root); add PATH adds that repo; relative PATH is made absolute against the working directory (Env.Getwd); a PATH without .adjudicate.json exits 1 and writes nothing; adding a listed path again is a no-op (exit 0, file unchanged byte for byte).
- remove PATH removes it; removing a path not listed exits 1 (or is a no-op: decide under C32 and test it); list after each operation.
- list on a missing file prints nothing (JSON: {"repos": []}) and exits 0; list --json shape pinned.
- A malformed config file (bad JSON, unknown key, relative path) makes every repos command exit 1 naming the file, and add/remove do not overwrite it.
- Save is atomic: no temp file is left behind; the directory is created.
- Usage errors (unknown subcommand, extra argument, blank PATH) exit 2.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Decide under C32 and record as slicer notes on S38: package placement; what --root means for repos (recommend: the default PATH for add, else unused); removing an unlisted path (recommend exit 1); whether list marks repos whose path no longer holds .adjudicate.json (recommend: not in this slice; S18 warns); path comparison (cleaned absolute string, no symlink resolution).
2. Red tests, then the code, following the existing command split (cli parses, commands acts, render prints).
3. Docs as in Files.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- . scripts/env.sh; go test ./...; go vet ./...; gofmt -l cmd internal prints nothing.
- go build -o .cache/bin/adj ./cmd/adj; with XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<worktree>/.cache/tmp/s38-check: adj repos add --root <worktree>, adj repos list, adj repos list --json, adj repos remove <worktree> behave as documented. Never run it against the real home config.
- .cache/bin/adj lint --root . is clean; mutation check each new test; slicer check --json is clean.
